title: Healthy Lifestyle 4: Drugs, Alcohol and Smoking
subject: Biology
description: Medicinal and recreational drugs, addiction, alcohol and pregnancy, and how the chemicals in tobacco smoke damage health.
author: L.M.

cards.back:
A chemical substance that affects the way your body works

(Drugs alter the chemical reactions inside your body.)
A drug used in medicine that benefits your health

A drug taken for enjoyment, to relax or to stay awake

(They usually have no health benefits and are often harmful.)

Painkillers, antibiotics, antihistamines

(e.g. paracetamol is a painkiller.)

cards.front: What are antibiotics used to treat?
cards.back:
Bacterial infections

(e.g. chest infections.)

Yes, if not taken the right way

(Some also have unwanted side effects.)

Heroin, cocaine, cannabis

(Ecstasy is also illegal.)
Alcohol, tobacco, caffeine

cards.front: Is caffeine a medicinal or a recreational drug?
cards.back:
Recreational

(It is a stimulant that speeds up your nervous system.)
When your body depends on a drug and you need to keep taking it to feel normal

Unpleasant effects when an addicted person stops taking a drug

(e.g. headaches, anxiety and sweating. They make it harder to give up.)

A drug that speeds up the nervous system

(e.g. caffeine, nicotine.)

A drug that slows down the nervous system

(e.g. alcohol.)

cards.front: Which drug is found in alcoholic drinks?
cards.back:
Ethanol

(It is absorbed into the blood and travels to the brain, where it affects the nervous system.)
A person with an addiction to alcohol

cards.front: What is one unit of alcohol?
cards.back: 10 ml (10 cm³) of pure alcohol

cards.front: How many units of alcohol are in a pint of lager?
cards.back:
3

(A glass of wine is 2, an alcopop 1.5, a shot of vodka 1.)

cards.front: As someone drinks more and more alcohol, what happens? (in order)
cards.back: Relaxed, then loses muscle control, slurred speech, blurred vision, unconsciousness, death

Short-term heavy drinking

(It can cause a headache [hangover], vomiting, or even needing the stomach pumped in hospital.)

cards.front: What can drinking a lot of alcohol over a long time cause?
cards.back: Stomach ulcers, heart disease, brain and liver damage

Scarring of the liver, so it works less well

(The liver breaks down ethanol, so heavy drinkers' livers get scarred. It can cause death.)

cards.front: What is a safe amount of alcohol to drink during pregnancy?
cards.back: None (there is no safe amount)

cards.front: How does alcohol reach an unborn baby?
cards.back:
It crosses the placenta into the baby's (foetus's) bloodstream

(It can then damage the developing organs and brain.)

cards.front: Drinking alcohol in pregnancy increases the risk of...
cards.back: Miscarriage, stillbirth, premature birth and low birth weight
Fetal Alcohol Syndrome

cards.front: What does Fetal Alcohol Syndrome do?
cards.back:
Affects how the baby's brain develops

(It can cause learning difficulties, facial problems and a poor immune system. It cannot be cured or outgrown.)
Get pregnant
The ability to get pregnant

cards.front: Why should people trying to get pregnant avoid alcohol?
cards.back:
Alcohol reduces fertility, and they might drink before they know they are pregnant

(e.g. alcohol makes men produce less sperm.)

An addictive stimulant that affects the brain

(It makes the heart beat faster and narrows blood vessels.)

A sticky black carcinogen that collects in the lungs

(It irritates and narrows the airways and causes cancer.)
A substance that causes cancer

cards.front: Carbon monoxide: what does it do?
cards.back:
Stops the blood carrying as much oxygen

(It is a poisonous gas that binds to red blood cells in place of oxygen.)
Dust particles in smoke that damage the cilia

cards.front: Why do smokers cough a lot?
cards.back:
Smoke stops the cilia sweeping mucus out of the airways, so mucus flows into the lungs and is coughed up

(This also makes infections more likely.)

A lung disease where the alveoli walls are weakened and burst

(Less oxygen gets into the blood, so the person is breathless.)

cards.front: How does smoking cause heart disease?
cards.back:
It makes the arteries become blocked

(This can cause a heart attack or stroke.)
Breathing in other people's cigarette smoke

cards.front: How can smoking during pregnancy harm the baby?
cards.back:
Higher risk of miscarriage and low birth weight

(It also affects the baby's development. Parents smoking after birth increases the risk of cot death.)

cards.front: Name three short-term effects of smoking.
cards.back:
Awful breath, a continuous cough, yellow teeth and fingers

(Also less taste and smell.)

cards.front: Name three long-term effects of smoking.
cards.back:
Cancers, heart disease, lung diseases

(Also circulation problems and premature ageing.)

cards.front: Air goes into the lungs through which tubes, in order?
cards.back: Trachea, bronchus, bronchioles, alveoli

questions.question: Which of these is a medicinal drug?
questions.explanation: Antibiotics are used in medicine to treat bacterial infections.

questions.question: Why do people take recreational drugs?
options: To treat pain prescribed by a doctor
For enjoyment, to relax or stay awake
questions.explanation: Recreational drugs are taken for enjoyment and usually have no health benefits.

questions.question: Which of these drugs is illegal?
questions.explanation: Cocaine, heroin, cannabis and ecstasy are illegal. Caffeine and alcohol are legal recreational drugs.

questions.question: What are withdrawal symptoms?
options: Unpleasant effects when an addicted person stops taking a drug
questions.explanation: Withdrawal symptoms such as headaches, anxiety and sweating make it harder to give up a drug.

questions.question: Alcohol is a depressant. What does that mean?
options: It slows down the nervous system
It speeds up the nervous system
questions.explanation: Depressants slow down the nervous system and your body's reactions.

questions.question: Which of these is a stimulant?
questions.explanation: Caffeine and nicotine are stimulants: they speed up the nervous system.

questions.question: Which drug is found in alcoholic drinks?
questions.explanation: Alcoholic drinks contain ethanol.

questions.question: One unit of alcohol is...
questions.explanation: One unit is 10 ml (10 cm³) of pure alcohol. A pint of lager is about 3 units.

questions.question: Long-term heavy drinking can scar the liver. What is this called?
questions.explanation: Cirrhosis is scarring of the liver. The liver then works less well and it can cause death.

questions.question: What is a safe amount of alcohol to drink during pregnancy?
questions.explanation: There is no safe amount. Alcohol crosses the placenta and can damage the baby's organs and brain.

questions.question: True or false: all children whose mothers drink will develop FAS.
questions.explanation: False. Drinking increases the risk, but not every child will develop FAS.

questions.question: True or false: you can tell if someone has FAS just by looking at them.
questions.explanation: False. FAS mainly affects how the brain develops.

questions.question: True or false: it is possible to cure or outgrow FAS.
questions.explanation: False. FAS cannot be cured or outgrown.

questions.question: True or false: alcohol affects fertility in both men and women.
questions.explanation: True. For example, alcohol makes men produce less sperm.

questions.question: Which chemical in tobacco smoke makes people addicted?
questions.explanation: Nicotine is an addictive stimulant that affects the brain.

questions.question: Which chemical in tobacco smoke is a carcinogen that collects in the lungs?
questions.explanation: Tar is a sticky black carcinogen: it causes cancer.

questions.question: Carbon monoxide is harmful because it...
options: reduces the oxygen the blood can carry
questions.explanation: Carbon monoxide binds to red blood cells in place of oxygen.

questions.question: What do the cilia in your airways do?
options: Sweep mucus out of the airways
questions.explanation: Cilia sweep mucus (with trapped dirt and microorganisms) away. Smoke stops them working.

questions.question: What is passive smoking?
questions.explanation: Passive smoking increases the risk of circulatory and respiratory conditions.

questions.question: Which is a long-term effect of smoking?
questions.explanation: Heart disease is a long-term effect. The others are short-term effects.
